cells.tense: You are here with the pen while something inside you stays open and nothing has been poured yet.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Notice a pull this week and take a step toward it before you decide whether it's good for you.
cells.core:
You can let something tug at you and not turn it into a decision. That's the skill — feeling the pull before naming what it is for. In the half-lit rooms, where the next step gets chosen, you stay available long enough for the pull to become real, and the room feels it. You don't rush yourself shut.
Catch a pull this week and follow it a little. Not to the end. One step. Something you might want to make, say, or touch. Feel what being drawn is like, and hold off deciding whether it's good for you. The decision can wait. The pull won't wait as long. Move on one and you'll learn what the feeling was there for — nothing else needs settling yet.
cells.sheetLine: You can follow a pull without making it mean anything.
cells.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
cells.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen

cells.tense: You are braced for a feeling that has not arrived yet, and the bracing has become the work.
cells.ask: Stay with a piece of work you started until it holds up by itself, then stop and set it down.
cells.core:
Where something in you is open, too much is held ready. Every possible feeling gets pre-felt, pre-planned, pre-answered, so none can arrive when they choose. You reach the moment before it reaches you, guarding against it. It looks like care and runs like strain — you finish other people's sentences about what you will feel.
Stay with a piece of work you started until it holds up by itself. A draft, a repair, a plan someone else can carry through. Not perfect — finished. Don't wait for a feeling to confirm it was the right thing. The feeling is the part you keep reaching for. The standing part is what you can set down. Finish it, then take your hands off it.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish something instead of bracing for it.
cells.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
cells.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen

cells.tense: You are still at a door that has swung shut, one hand out for a feeling that hasn't come.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Stop imagining what you began and make the next real move with it now — let it carry the size it takes.
cells.core:
In the half-lit rooms lately, not much gets taken in. What could draw you passes by unclaimed. You can name what things are; letting them be more than that isn't happening right now. That's not a flaw in you. The room at the end is empty and standing where you are is easier than walking in.
Stop planning what you began and make the next real move with it now. Not imagining it. Making it. The size is whatever it is. The point is the door on this side, where you hand what you have forward. Small and actual beats possible and untouched. Once it has some size, you'll see whether you wanted it — and if you didn't, drop it. The handing was the point.
cells.sheetLine: You can let something you started actually get bigger.
cells.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
cells.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen

cells.tense: You are steering without a hand on the wheel, in a room you keep saying you didn't pick.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When someone gives you something for what you gave, receive it and say a plain thank-you.
cells.core:
Your openings are yours. You've been filing them under circumstance, under the room, under someone else's draw. What you actually do is notice first, make it safe, and let something arrive at its own pace. That's a contribution, and you've been leaving it unsigned.
Let one exchange run both ways this week. Not a tally — one return. Someone hands you something for what you gave: a thanks, their time, a seat at the table, a favor. Receive it and don't wave it off, and when it lands, say thank you and mean it. Watch what comes back; that's how you see what you've been giving. If nothing comes back, note it. That's information, not a verdict on you.
cells.sheetLine: The openings were yours. Let one come back.
cells.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
cells.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen
